editorial.tldr: Late October brought three Show HN projects pitching a control room or control plane for LLM agents: God, flightdeck, and Omneum. On Nov 4 the vLLM blog introduced Kinference, an open source inference control plane for vLLM on Kubernetes.
editorial.whats_new: OpenAI published two Control Room posts on Nov 9: a central system that tracks model workloads across its research infrastructure and can rapidly stop them when safety or security concerns arise.
editorial.why_it_matters: The label now spans three layers: agent observability, inference serving, and kill-switch control over training and research workloads. Check which layer a "control plane" actually governs before adopting it.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run vLLM on Kubernetes, evaluate Kinference for per-tenant rate limits and cost tracking in a staging cluster. Treat the Show HN agent tools as early experiments and OpenAI's Control Room as a design reference, not something you can deploy.

status.detail: Independent projects keep using "control plane" or "control room" for different layers; OpenAI's Control Room is the latest and an internal system, not a product.
